question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The chairman expressed (a)/ his sincere thank (b)/ to all the volunteers for their efforts. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Thanks" (an expression of gratitude) is a noun that is always used in the plural form. The singular "thank" is only a verb (I thank you), so "his sincere thank" must be "his sincere thanks".

◦ Corrected sentence: The chairman expressed his sincere thanks to all the volunteers for their efforts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The chairman expressed" is a proper subject–verb pair in the simple past.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "to all the volunteers for their efforts" is a proper prepositional phrase, and "their" agrees with the plural "volunteers".

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "thank" in part (b) is incorrect.

 

NOTE

 

• Plural-only nouns: thanks, congratulations, regards, greetings, wages, riches, proceeds, belongings, surroundings. The verb form remains singular: thank (verb) but thanks (noun).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The volunteers (a)/ took great pain (b)/ to make the event (c)/ a grand success. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the idiom "take pains" (to make a careful, hard effort), the noun "pains" is always used in the plural. The singular "pain" means physical or mental suffering and does not fit the meaning here.

◦ Corrected sentence: The volunteers took great pains to make the event a grand success.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The volunteers" is a proper plural subject.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "to make the event" is a proper infinitive phrase showing purpose.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "a grand success" is a proper noun phrase acting as the object complement of "make".

 

NOTE

 

• Idioms with plural-only nouns: take pains, make amends, give thanks, in high spirits, come to terms, be on good terms, lose one's bearings.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

A new principle (a)/ was appointed by the governing council (b)/ for the girls' college (c)/ in the city. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Principal" means the head of a school or college, while "principle" means a basic rule or belief. Since a person is being appointed, the correct noun is "principal".

◦ Corrected sentence: A new principal was appointed by the governing council for the girls' college in the city.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "was appointed by the governing council" is a proper passive construction with a singular verb.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "girls' college" correctly shows plural possession (a college for girls).

 

• Part (d) is correct — "in the city" is a proper prepositional phrase of place.

 

NOTE

 

• Confusable nouns: principal / principle, stationary / stationery, complement / compliment, personnel / personal, council / counsel, site / sight / cite.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The polices (a)/ have arrested (b)/ the gang members. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Police" is a collective noun that is always plural in meaning and takes a plural verb. It has no plural form "polices", so the correct phrase is "The police".

◦ Corrected sentence: The police have arrested the gang members.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — the plural verb "have arrested" agrees with the plural noun "police".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "the gang members" is a proper object, and the noun modifier "gang" stays singular.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "polices" in part (a) is incorrect.

 

NOTE

 

• Nouns that are plural in meaning but have no "-s": police, cattle, people, poultry, folk, clergy, gentry. Say The police are, Cattle graze, These people — never polices, cattles, peoples (unless "peoples" means nations).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Everyone in the colony (a)/ knows that the new car (b)/ parked outside belongs to (c)/ my brother's-in-law son. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the possessive of a compound noun, the apostrophe and "s" are added to the last word of the compound: brother-in-law's. So "brother's-in-law son" must be "brother-in-law's son".

◦ Corrected sentence: Everyone in the colony knows that the new car parked outside belongs to my brother-in-law's son.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Everyone" takes a singular verb, and the phrase "in the colony" is a proper prepositional phrase.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "knows that the new car" agrees with the singular subject "Everyone".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "parked outside" is a proper past participle phrase modifying "car", followed by the correct verb "belongs to".

 

NOTE

 

• Possessive of compounds: son-in-law's, mother-in-law's, commander-in-chief's, editor-in-chief's, passer-by's. Plural possessive: sons-in-law's (rarely asked).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The company (a)/ has launched a (b)/ three-years warranty (c)/ on all its products. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a number + noun joins to form a hyphenated adjective before another noun, the noun stays singular — it does not take "-s". So "three-years warranty" must be "three-year warranty".

◦ Corrected sentence: The company has launched a three-year warranty on all its products.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The company" is a proper singular subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "has launched a" is the correct present perfect for a singular subject, and "a" agrees with the singular "warranty".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "on all its products" is a proper prepositional phrase, and "its" agrees with the singular "company".

 

NOTE

 

• a three-year warranty but a warranty of three years; a five-day week but a week of five days; a 100-metre race; a two-hour drive.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The benefits of regular yoga (a)/ include better flexibility, (b)/ improved concentration (c)/ and to reduce stress. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Items in a list must be in the same grammatical form (parallelism). "Better flexibility" and "improved concentration" are noun phrases, so the last item must also be a noun phrase — "reduced stress" — not the infinitive "to reduce stress".

◦ Corrected sentence: The benefits of regular yoga include better flexibility, improved concentration and reduced stress.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The benefits of regular yoga" is a proper plural subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — the plural verb "include" agrees with the plural subject "benefits", and "better flexibility" is a noun phrase.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "improved concentration" is a noun phrase that matches the list.

 

NOTE

 

• Nouns in a series must have the same form: She likes reading, writing and painting (not to paint); the speed, the strength and the courage of the team.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The laboratory report (a)/ revealed the presence of (b)/ harmful bacterias (c)/ in the drinking water. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Bacteria" is already the plural of the Latin noun "bacterium". Adding "-s" to it gives the incorrect form "bacterias". The correct phrase is "harmful bacteria".

◦ Corrected sentence: The laboratory report revealed the presence of harmful bacteria in the drinking water.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The laboratory report" is a proper singular subject, and "laboratory" acts as a noun modifier.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "revealed the presence of" is a proper simple past verb phrase with the correct preposition.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "in the drinking water" is a proper prepositional phrase of place.

 

NOTE

 

• Latin/Greek plurals: bacterium–bacteria, datum–data, medium–media, phenomenon–phenomena, criterion–criteria, curriculum–curricula, crisis–crises, analysis–analyses. Never add another "-s" to these plurals.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The volunteers gave (a)/ free sewing machines to (b)/ the womens of the village. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Women" is the irregular plural of "woman". It is already plural, so adding "-s" to it is wrong. The correct phrase is "the women of the village".

◦ Corrected sentence: The volunteers gave free sewing machines to the women of the village.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The volunteers gave" is a proper subject and verb in the simple past.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "free sewing machines to" is a proper object with the correct preposition, and "sewing" is a noun modifier.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "womens" in part (c) is incorrect.

 

NOTE

 

• Irregular plurals that never take another "-s": men, women, children, feet, teeth, geese, mice, lice, oxen. Their possessives take an apostrophe: women's, children's, men's.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The film is (a)/ based on Ravi's and Sunita's (b)/ joint novel, which (c)/ won several awards. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When two or more persons jointly own the same thing, only the last noun takes the possessive ('s). Since the novel is a joint work, the phrase must be "Ravi and Sunita's joint novel".

◦ Corrected sentence: The film is based on Ravi and Sunita's joint novel, which won several awards.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The film is" is a proper singular subject and verb in the present tense.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "joint novel, which" is a proper noun phrase followed by a correct relative pronoun for a thing.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "won several awards" is a proper simple past predicate with a plural object.

 

NOTE

 

• Ram and Shyam's shop (joint) but Ram's and Shyam's shops (separate ownership).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The teacher was upset by (a)/ his repeated absents (b)/ from the class (c)/ during the exam week. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Absent" is an adjective (he is absent) or a verb. After the possessive "his repeated", a noun is required, and the noun is "absences" (plural, because of "repeated").

◦ Corrected sentence: The teacher was upset by his repeated absences from the class during the exam week.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The teacher was upset by" is a proper passive-type adjectival phrase with the correct preposition.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "from the class" is a proper prepositional phrase with the correct preposition after "absences".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "during the exam week" is a proper prepositional phrase of time, with "exam" acting as a noun modifier.

 

NOTE

 

• Adjective–noun pairs: absent–absence, present–presence, silent–silence, ignorant–ignorance, patient–patience, important–importance, different–difference, brave–bravery.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Many livestocks (a)/ died in the (b)/ severe drought that (c)/ hit the region last year. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Livestock" is a collective noun that has no plural form; it takes a plural verb but never "-s". So "livestocks" must be "livestock".

◦ Corrected sentence: Many livestock died in the severe drought that hit the region last year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "died in the" is a proper simple past verb with the correct preposition.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "severe drought that" is a proper noun phrase followed by a correct relative pronoun for a thing.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "hit the region last year" is a proper past-tense predicate ("hit" is the same in past and present).

 

NOTE

 

• Same in singular and plural / no "-s": livestock, cattle, poultry, deer, sheep, fish, series, species, offspring, aircraft, crossroads.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The shopkeeper showed us (a)/ all the new models (b)/ of sofas and (c)/ furnitures in his showroom. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Furniture" is an uncountable noun. It has no plural form, so "furnitures" is wrong. For a countable sense, use "pieces of furniture".

◦ Corrected sentence: The shopkeeper showed us all the new models of sofas and furniture in his showroom.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The shopkeeper showed us" is a proper subject, verb and indirect object in the simple past.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "all the new models" is a proper noun phrase, and "models" is a correct plural.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "of sofas and" is correct because "sofa" is a countable noun that takes "-s".

 

NOTE

 

• Uncountable nouns that Indian learners often pluralise: furniture, luggage, baggage, machinery, equipment, scenery, stationery, jewellery, mail, cutlery, hair, advice.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The residents complained (a)/ to the municipal officers (b)/ about the frequent (c)/ interrupt in water supply. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Interrupt" is a verb. After the adjective "frequent" and before the preposition "in", a noun is required. Since "frequent" shows repeated events, the correct noun is the plural "interruptions".

◦ Corrected sentence: The residents complained to the municipal officers about the frequent interruptions in water supply.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The residents complained" is a proper plural subject and verb in the simple past.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "to the municipal officers" is a proper prepositional phrase, and "complained to" is the correct pattern.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "about the frequent" correctly follows "complained" and introduces the noun phrase.

 

NOTE

 

• Verb–noun pairs: interrupt–interruption, complain–complaint, discover–discovery, fail–failure, admit–admission, permit–permission, arrange–arrangement, marry–marriage.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The children were thrilled (a)/ by such an amusing tricks (b)/ performed by the magician (c)/ at the party. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The article "an" is used only before a singular countable noun. "Tricks" is plural, so "an" cannot be used. The correct phrase is "such amusing tricks" (or "such an amusing trick").

◦ Corrected sentence: The children were thrilled by such amusing tricks performed by the magician at the party.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The children were thrilled" is a proper plural subject with the correct plural verb "were".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "performed by the magician" is a proper past participle phrase modifying "tricks".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "at the party" is a proper prepositional phrase of place.

 

NOTE

 

• Word order: such + a/an + adjective + singular noun (such an amusing trick); such + adjective + plural noun (such amusing tricks).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

On dry pitches, (a)/ the team's pace attack (b)/ is a perfect compliment (c)/ to its spin department. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Complement" means something that completes or goes well with something else, while "compliment" means an expression of praise. Since the pace attack goes well with the spin department, the correct noun is "complement".

◦ Corrected sentence: On dry pitches, the team's pace attack is a perfect complement to its spin department.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "On dry pitches," is a proper introductory prepositional phrase.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the team's pace attack" shows correct possession, and "pace" acts as a noun modifier.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "to its spin department" is a proper prepositional phrase, and "its" agrees with the singular "team".

 

NOTE

 

• Complement (completes) vs compliment (praise); Principal vs principle; Stationary vs stationery; Personal vs personnel; Advice (noun) vs advise (verb).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

Because of heavy rain, (a)/ only two-third of (b)/ the crop could be harvested. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In fractions, the numerator is a cardinal number and the denominator is an ordinal number. When the numerator is greater than one, the denominator takes "-s": "two-thirds", not "two-third".

◦ Corrected sentence: Because of heavy rain, only two-thirds of the crop could be harvested.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Because of heavy rain," is a proper introductory phrase giving the reason.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "the crop could be harvested" is a proper passive construction, and the singular "crop" agrees with the verb.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "two-third" in part (b) is incorrect.

 

NOTE

 

• one-third, two-thirds, three-fourths, five-eighths. After "of + singular noun", the verb is singular; after "of + plural noun", the verb is plural.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The contractor said (a)/ the repairs would need (b)/ two and a half day (c)/ to be completed. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A noun that follows a numeral greater than one, including "two and a half", must be in the plural. So "two and a half day" must be "two and a half days".

◦ Corrected sentence: The contractor said the repairs would need two and a half days to be completed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The contractor said" is a proper subject and reporting verb in the simple past.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the repairs would need" is a proper reported clause with "would" for the past-tense reporting.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "to be completed" is a proper passive infinitive.

 

NOTE

 

• one and a half hours, two and a half years, one and a quarter kilometres; but the noun is singular for up to one: half a day, one day, a quarter of a mile.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The new airport is (a)/ under construction (b)/ near the highway (c)/ on the outskirt of the city. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Outskirts" (the outer parts of a city) is a noun that is always used in the plural form. So "the outskirt of the city" must be "the outskirts of the city".

◦ Corrected sentence: The new airport is under construction near the highway on the outskirts of the city.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The new airport is" is a proper singular subject and verb in the present tense.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "under construction" is a proper prepositional phrase meaning "being built".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "near the highway" is a proper prepositional phrase of place.

 

NOTE

 

• Always plural: outskirts, surroundings, belongings, savings, earnings, premises, remains, riches, proceeds, arrears, thanks, trousers, scissors, spectacles.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The childrens' education (a)/ is the first priority (b)/ of the new (c)/ government's policy. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Children" is an irregular plural that does not end in "s". Its possessive is formed by adding "'s", not just an apostrophe. So "childrens'" must be "children's".

◦ Corrected sentence: The children's education is the first priority of the new government's policy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — the singular verb "is" agrees with the singular subject "education".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "of the new" is a proper prepositional phrase with an adjective introducing the noun.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "government's policy" correctly shows singular possession.

 

NOTE

 

• Plurals not ending in "s" take 's: children's, men's, women's, people's. Plurals ending in "s" take only the apostrophe: boys', girls', teachers', engineers'.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Two major economic crisises (a)/ have hit the country (b)/ within a decade (c)/ and slowed its growth. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nouns ending in "-is" of Greek origin change to "-es" in the plural: crisis → crises. "Crisises" is an incorrect double plural.

◦ Corrected sentence: Two major economic crises have hit the country within a decade and slowed its growth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — the plural verb "have hit" agrees with the plural subject "crises".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "within a decade" is a proper prepositional phrase of time.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "and slowed its growth" is a proper past-tense predicate, and "its" agrees with the singular "country".

 

NOTE

 

• -is → -es: crisis–crises, analysis–analyses, basis–bases, thesis–theses, hypothesis–hypotheses, oasis–oases, parenthesis–parentheses, axis–axes.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

During the rescue, (a)/ everyone was amazed (b)/ by the young soldier's (c)/ sheer brave. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Brave" is an adjective. After the possessive "soldier's" and the adjective "sheer", a noun is required. The noun form of "brave" is "bravery".

◦ Corrected sentence: During the rescue, everyone was amazed by the young soldier's sheer bravery.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "During the rescue," is a proper introductory prepositional phrase of time.

 

• Part (b) is correct — the singular verb "was amazed" agrees with the singular subject "everyone".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "by the young soldier's" is a proper phrase with the correct possessive form.

 

NOTE

 

• Adjective–noun pairs: brave–bravery, wise–wisdom, proud–pride, strong–strength, long–length, high–height, deep–depth, wide–width, true–truth.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The news of his (a)/ sudden death (b)/ were shocking (c)/ for the entire village. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "News" ends in "-s" but is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb. So "were shocking" must be "was shocking".

◦ Corrected sentence: The news of his sudden death was shocking for the entire village.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The news of his" is a proper noun phrase with the correct possessive adjective.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "sudden death" is a proper adjective + noun phrase.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "for the entire village" is a proper prepositional phrase after "shocking".

 

NOTE

 

• Plural in form but singular in meaning: news, physics, mathematics, economics, politics, ethics, measles, mumps, billiards, athletics. Always use a singular verb: Mathematics is, The news is.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The farmer (a)/ bought two machineries (b)/ from the fair (c)/ last week. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Machinery" is an uncountable collective noun, so it has no plural form. For individual items, use the countable noun "machines" (or "pieces of machinery").

◦ Corrected sentence: The farmer bought two machines from the fair last week.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The farmer" is a proper singular subject.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "from the fair" is a proper prepositional phrase of place.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "last week" is a proper adverb phrase of time, used with the simple past "bought".

 

NOTE

 

• Uncountable nouns with countable partners: machinery–machines, furniture–pieces of furniture, luggage–bags, jewellery–ornaments, scenery–views, information–facts.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

A months leave (a)/ was granted to him (b)/ by the officer (c)/ on medical grounds. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nouns denoting time (day, week, month, year) take the possessive ('s) when they show duration or measure before another noun. Since "month" is singular (because of "A"), the phrase must be "A month's leave".

◦ Corrected sentence: A month's leave was granted to him by the officer on medical grounds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — the singular verb "was granted" agrees with the singular subject "leave", and "to him" is correct.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "by the officer" is a proper agent phrase in the passive voice.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "on medical grounds" is a proper prepositional phrase, and "grounds" (reasons) is a correct plural.

 

NOTE

 

• Possessives of time and measure: a month's leave, a week's notice, today's news, yesterday's match, a stone's throw, ten minutes' walk.
